title: Correct acceleration value
description: Essential: The student must correctly calculate the acceleration as 4 m/s² using kinematic equations.

title: Correct normal force value
description: Essential: The student must correctly calculate the normal force/pressure on snow as 650 N using mg cosθ.

title: Kinematic equation application
description: Important: The student must correctly apply the uniformly accelerated motion equation (x = v₀t + ½at² or equivalent) to find acceleration.

title: Force decomposition on incline
description: Important: The student must correctly resolve gravitational force into components parallel and perpendicular to the slope.

title: Newton's second law application
description: Important: The student must apply Newton's second law along the slope (mg sinθ - f = ma) to find resistance.

title: Newton's third law recognition
description: Optional: The student should recognize that the pressure on snow equals the normal force by Newton's third law.

title: Unit consistency
description: Optional: The student should include correct units (m/s², N) with numerical answers.

title: Sign error in kinematics
description: Pitfall: Using incorrect sign convention in kinematic equations leading to wrong acceleration sign or magnitude.

title: Confusing force components
description: Pitfall: Using sinθ instead of cosθ for normal force, or vice versa for parallel component.

title: Forgetting Newton's third law
description: Pitfall: Stating the normal force (650 N) as the snow's force but not identifying it as the pressure on snow.
